newsitem.title: THAILAND: Airlines cancel flights to Phnom Penh.
newsitem.headline: Airlines cancel flights to Phnom Penh.

text.p: The major airlines that fly into Phnom Penh have cancelled all flights to the Cambodian capital for Saturday and maybe Sunday due to the current tense political situation, airline employees said.

"Both of our flights today were cancelled and they will be cancelled tomorrow also," a Royal Air Cambodge ticket agent in Bangkok told Reuters. "It is because of the political problem there, and we fear for our passenger's safety."
She said there was a possibility the flights would also be stopped on Monday.
Thai Airways, the other major airline serving the Phnom Penh airport, also cancelled its flights on Saturday after fighting broke out at a base just a few kilometres from the airport.
"You will have to check tomorrow morning to see about the flights tomorrow," said Usankorn Kitbanroon, ticket agent for Thai Airways at the Bangkok airport.
"We decided today it would be better to cancel our flights because there are problems there," she said.
A Reuter cameraman on flight TG696 on Saturday morning said the plane had almost arrived in Phnom Penh when it was told to return to Bangkok.

At least one Vietnam Airlines flight took off from Phnom Penh in the afternoon, Cambodian airline sources said. Fighting resumed near the airport shortly after and it was not clear if any other planes were able to leave.
A security official at the Phnom Penh airport told Reuters that airport officials had not yet decided if they would open the airport on Sunday. He said the decision would be taken in the morning.
Troops loyal to Cambodia's rival prime ministers, who head a fractured coalition government, clashed on the northwestern outsirts of Phnom Penh early on Sunday at a base near the airport.
Fighting continued sporadically throughout the day and fresh clashes broke out as darkness fell in the capital.
